History:
- 3-day history of acute diarrhoea, initially watery now very loose; ≥4 bowel motions today (lost count overall).
- Associated vomiting since onset; unable to retain water, tea, or other liquids. Last emesis ≈2 hours before call (after breakfast).
- Subjective fever (“literally boiling”); no thermometer reading available.
- Periumbilical abdominal pain/tenderness; pain precedes urge to defecate and is episodic.
- No visible blood in stool or urine.
- Urinating normally; last void ≈1 hour prior to consult; colour not observed.
- No rash, no previous similar gastrointestinal episodes.
- Possible infectious contact: brother with identical symptoms, reports outbreak at his school. No recent travel.
- Diet normally balanced; currently attempting home ORS (salt-sugar mix) ×3/day for 2 days without improvement.
- Triggers/relievers: none identified; vomiting limits oral intake.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: none reported.
- Surgical history: none.
- Gynecologic: Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; uses no contraception; not sexually active.
- Medications:
  • Vitamin D daily (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • Ibuprofen PRN for dysmenorrhoea (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • Oral rehydration solution (homemade) three times daily.
- Allergies: not discussed/missing.
- Social: Non-smoker; occasional alcohol (“a pint from time to time”). Lives with mother and brother. Works as a graphic designer; working from home today due to illness.

Physical Examination:
(telephone consultation – limited)
- General: Patient alert and oriented, able to converse.
- Reported fever (subjective).
- Abdomen: self-reported marked tenderness around umbilicus.
- Skin: no rash.
- GU: passing urine regularly; no haematuria.
- No other systemic findings elicited.

Impression:
Acute infectious gastroenteritis with ongoing vomiting, risk of dehydration; bacterial etiology to be excluded.

Management Plan:
- Continue oral rehydration salts; take tiny frequent sips to improve tolerance.
- Dietary advice: bland foods only (e.g., toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, dairy until settled.
- Arrange urgent clinic appointment today for:
  • Hydration assessment.  
  • Stool sample collection and culture to rule out bacterial infection.  
- Safety-net: If worsening symptoms, inability to pass urine, persistent vomiting, or concern about dehydration, attend A&E immediately and/or call back.
- Clinic booking to be made through support line; urgent slot requested.

Patient Summary:
Barbara, 38-year-old woman with 3-day history of profuse diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and subjective fever after contact with brother with similar illness. Likely viral gastroenteritis, but stool culture and in-person hydration check arranged to rule out bacterial cause and assess severity.

Key Takeaways:
1. Keep sipping ORS continuously; small amounts prevent vomiting.
2. Eat only bland food; avoid produce and dairy until diarrhoea resolves.
3. Seek urgent care if vomiting worsens, urine output drops, or feeling faint.

Next Steps:
- Attend urgent clinic appointment today for examination, hydration status, and stool sample.
- Follow stool culture results; consider targeted antibiotics if bacterial pathogen identified.
- Continue monitoring fluid intake/output; follow up via telephone if no improvement within 48 hours.
